inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share award expense' RMB33,247k (1368.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:5263); no cash taxes on equity awards are paid (awards are satisfied from treasury shares held by the trustee), so EquityAwardTaxes = 0. H1 FY2026 expense was RMB42,885k for the half under the new 2025 Share Award Scheme (1368.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2528), which is why the forward SBC path (0.55% -> 0.40% of revenue) sits above the FY2025 actual of 0.23%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows are RMB (CNY); the HKEX quote is HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1727 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T08:08Z; inverse HKDCNY=X printed 0.8518 (1/0.8518 = 1.1740, ties within 0.1%). Xtep has no dual listing to parity-check against, so the inverse-pair tie is the check. Per-share values are computed in RMB by the engine and converted to HKD with this rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD so they compare to current_price. refresh_price.py does not move this rate; re-derive it on any later refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z (HKEX regular close 16:08 HKT; not an after-hours print)
inputs.share_count_basis: If-converted. 2,815,096,985 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim note 22) less ~90.7m treasury shares held by the share-award trustee gives ~2,724.4m outstanding (equal to the H1 FY2026 basic weighted average, interim note 10, which is the only ex-treasury figure the filing prints; in-period issuance was 9.0m shares so the proxy is within 0.3%). Plus 266.4m conversion shares from the three outstanding Xtep Convertible Bonds: 2021 CB 70,150,398 @ HK$7.9385 (FY2025 AR:4403), 2024 CB 117,782,973 @ HK$5.2323 (AR:4446), 2026 CB 78,492,935 @ HK$6.37 (interim:1460). All three conversion prices are above the HK$3.645 market price but below the base/bull intrinsic values, so the bonds are treated as converted: their RMB1,272.0m carrying value is EXCLUDED from net debt and the shares are ADDED to the count. The 39.8m unvested share awards are NOT added: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charge once). The CSV's SharesOutstanding of 3,095.3m is the diluted weighted average (basic 2,724.4 + awards 39.8 + CB 331.1 at the H1 weighting) and is not used. Count held flat; buybacks nil since FY2021.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 June 2026 interim: cash and cash equivalents 3,449.0 + term deposits 600.0 (non-current) + 149.8 (current) + pledged deposits 36.0 = 4,234.8 of deposits and bank balances (company's own net-cash table, interim:1312-1319), less interest-bearing bank borrowings 520.6 + 116.4 = 637.0. Convertible bonds (1,272.0) are treated as converted (see share_count_basis) and lease liabilities (315.3) are excluded under lease treatment (B). The company's own 'net cash' of RMB2,325.8m deducts the CBs; ours is 3,597.8 before the 266.4m conversion shares.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% + beta ~1.05 x China equity risk premium ~7% (mature-market 4.3% + China country risk ~1.5% + HK-listed mid-cap consumer discretionary spread) = cost of equity ~9.2-9.5%; debt is immaterial (bank borrowings RMB637m vs RMB4.2bn deposits) so WACC = cost of equity, 9.5%. No further premium for core-brand cyclicality, DTC execution or governance: those are charged once, in the scenario paths and the 30% bear weight (adaptations rule f). Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal, financing section, + interest on lease liabilities, operating section) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path: FY2025 107.9 + 7.9 = 115.8m = 0.82% of revenue (AR:5280-5330); H1 FY2026 90.7 + 4.8 = 95.5m for the half, ~1.4% annualised, as 300-400 distributor stores a year convert to direct operation. Path 1.3% rising to 1.5%. Consequently lease liabilities (135.6 current + 179.7 non-current = 315.3) are excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 total D&A 297.5 less ROU 125.0 = 172.5m = 1.22% (PPE 167.5 + intangibles 5.0).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are RMB4.3m at 30 June 2026 (nil at FY2025) after the November 2024 disposal of KP Global; immaterial, no deduction and no leakage driver. FY0 NOPAT check: adj EBITDA 2,242.4 - SBC 33.2 - lease 115.8 - D&A ex-ROU 172.5 = EBIT 1,920.9 x (1 - 27.5%) = 1,392.7 vs reported attributable profit 1,371.6 -- ties within non-operating noise (financial income, CB interest, associates).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (operating company; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2: non-US consumer operating company, adaptations a/b/d applied). No prior DCF or memory entry; fresh build. EBITDA ANCHOR: FY2025 reported EBITDA 2,316.3 (operating profit 2,018.8 + D&A 297.5) + SBC 33.2 added back - 107.1 of financial income booked inside 'Other income and gains' within operating profit (income on term/structured deposits 43.8, FVOCI dividend 9.6, fair-value gain on 2021 CB derivative 22.0, fair-value gain on the KP Convertible Bond 31.7; AR note 5(ii):7337-7352) = adjusted EBITDA 2,242.4 = 15.85% of revenue. Those items are stripped because their source assets (deposits in net cash; FVOCI stakes, KP CB and associates in equity_bridge) are valued separately (matching-asset rule). Subsidy income of 301.1m (2.1% of revenue, 261.3m in FY2024) and royalty/rental income are left in as recurring operating items. KP CONVERTIBLE BOND: the RMB1,022.3m 'financial asset at FVTPL' is NOT cash -- it is the 3.5% PIK convertible bond issued by KP Global (the K-Swiss/Palladium business sold to the controlling Ding family in Nov-2024) maturing 29 Nov 2032 (AR note 31:8981-8995). It is a related-party receivable whose recovery depends on a loss-making business and the family's credit; carried in the bridge at 70% of book. LAST_FCF: 618.8 = reported FCF 675.3 (OCF 952.4 - PPE 264.1 - intangibles 13.0) - SBC 33.2 - bank interest income 23.3, per contract; it is well below the component-built normalised owner FCF (~1,300m) because FY2025 absorbed ~805m of working capital (trade payables unwound 439.6m, inventories +240.2m, receivables +170.1m). The forward build charges working capital on revenue CHANGE at -35% capture (net operating working capital ~RMB4.8bn = 34% of revenue, receivable days 120-127, inventory days 105), so the structural receivables stretch is a bear-case axis rather than a base-case constant. BUYBACKS: none since FY2021; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by expensed SBC, not by repurchases. REVENUE CONTINUITY: FY2023 reported revenue 14,345.5 includes K-Swiss/Palladium; continuing-only FY2023 is 12,742.9, so FY2024 growth is +6.5% like-for-like and FY2025 +4.2%. CB TREATMENT MEMO: had the CBs been treated as debt instead (deduct 1,272.0, 2,724.4m shares) the base IV would be marginally higher than the if-converted figure, since the blended conversion price (~HK$6.3) is below the base IV; if-converted is the conservative choice and the right one whenever IV exceeds the strikes.

equity_bridge.note: 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet (interim:1993); share of profits of associates (FY2025 54.4m) sits below operating profit and is not in the modelled flows, so the asset is added at carrying value.
Two strategic PRC stakes (5% and 11%) at fair value, 30 June 2026 (interim:1995); FY2025 dividend of 9.6m stripped from the EBITDA anchor (matching-asset rule).

equity_bridge.item: KP Convertible Bond (receivable from KP Global / Ding family) at 70% of fair value
equity_bridge.note: Carried at RMB1,022.3m at 30 June 2026 (interim note 21:3075); 3.5% PIK, matures 29 Nov 2032, issued by the loss-making K-Swiss/Palladium business the controlling family bought in Nov-2024. 30% haircut for related-party credit risk and illiquidity; fair-value gains (31.7m FY2025) stripped from the EBITDA anchor.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year average revenue growth (-1.5% guided FY2026 recovering to 2-3%); historical CAGRs are not a usable forward proxy because FY2020-23 include the divested K-Swiss/Palladium business and FY2026 is guided down
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR 7.1% (3yr) exceeds reported revenue CAGR 3.05% by >30% relative: equity was lifted by the Feb-2025 placing (RMB455.7m) and treasury-share disposals (RMB228.9m) and revenue is depressed by the KP divestiture, so neither is a clean growth read. EPS 3yr CAGR 10.5% is flattered by the FY2024 exit of KP losses.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - bank interest income, applied to the whole history. The series is too volatile for a CAGR (negative in FY2018 and FY2021, swinging with distributor receivables and payables), so fcf CAGRs are null; the FY2023-25 average owner FCF is ~691m against average net income of ~1,213m (57% conversion), the gap being working-capital absorption during the 10%+/yr growth years. Revenue 5yr CAGR mixes KP-inclusive FY2020 with KP-excluded FY2025 and understates organic growth slightly; the 3yr figure is reported-basis (FY2022 includes KP).

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue -1.5% per the August guidance of a slight full-year decline (H1 -0.6%, Q3 headwinds). Adjusted EBITDA margin drops ~1.5pp to 14.3% as H1's 2.0pp operating-margin compression (platform fees, logistics, DTC ROU/staff costs) persists into H2, then recovers only to the FY2025 level of 15% by FY2030 as converted stores mature -- no margin expansion beyond what the company already earned. Growth re-accelerates to 2.5-3% in FY2028-30 (Saucony/Merrell at ~12% of revenue growing ~10%, core Xtep brand flat to +1%) and fades to 2% terminal. Lease cost rises to 1.5% of revenue with the DTC conversion; SBC runs at ~0.5% under the 2025 Share Award Scheme; cash tax 27.5% (25% PRC + dividend withholding on a >=50% payout). Terminal value capped at 13x year-10 owner FCF -- a structurally slow mass-market brand does not earn a 20x exit.

bull.narrative: The running franchise holds: core Xtep brand stabilises in FY2027 and grows low single digits as the 160X/QING YUN platforms and the Xtep Selected outlet format lift store productivity; Saucony re-accelerates to 15-20% on premium-mall expansion and lifestyle apparel, taking the professional segment to ~18% of revenue with its operating margin rising from 7% toward Xtep-brand levels; DTC conversion pays back from FY2028 (higher gross margin retained, receivable days falling, hence -30% capture). Group adjusted EBITDA margin reaches 16.5%, ~0.7pp above FY2025. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 15x. Same 9.5% WACC.

bear.narrative: The H1 FY2026 trend is the new run-rate: the core Xtep brand (87% of revenue) loses share to Anta/Li Ning above and 361 Degrees below, revenue falls 3% a year in FY2026-27 and does not recover to FY2025 levels within the horizon; Saucony decelerates to mid-single digits as Q2's low-single-digit growth showed. Discounting plus platform/logistics fees and the cost of running 300-400 converted stores a year compress the adjusted EBITDA margin to 12% by FY2028 and hold it there; distributor receivables keep stretching (-40% capture) and SBC stays at 0.6%. No solvency axis -- RMB3.6bn net cash and a 50% payout survive this path -- so the bear is an earnings-power case, not a going-concern one. Terminal growth 1.5%, cap 11x.

scenario_narratives.base: Guided FY2026 decline (-1.5%) with margins ~1.5pp below FY2025 as DTC transition costs and platform fees bite, then a slow recovery to the FY2025 margin level by FY2030 and 2-3% growth carried by Saucony/Merrell while the core brand drifts flat. Value rests on RMB3.6bn net cash plus a ~RMB1.3bn/yr normalised owner FCF capitalised at 13x.
scenario_narratives.bull: Core brand stabilises, Saucony scales to ~18% of revenue with a maturing margin, DTC conversion lifts gross-margin retention and shortens the receivables cycle; group adjusted EBITDA margin 16.5%, growth 3-5.5% through FY2031.
scenario_narratives.bear: Core brand decline persists (-3%/yr near term), discounting and channel costs take the margin to 12%, receivables keep absorbing cash; an earnings-power downgrade on a net-cash balance sheet.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the core brand that is 87% of revenue has turned negative, management cut FY2026 guidance to a decline in August, and Xtep is the only one of China's big-four listed sportswear names with both revenue and profit falling in H1 FY2026 -- the bear path is the current trend continuing, not a shock. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (core-brand stabilisation, Saucony re-acceleration after Q2's slowdown, and DTC payback on a timeline management has not given). Bear is not pushed higher because the balance sheet carries RMB3.6bn of net cash and no covenant or going-concern axis exists.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Xtep is valued as a mature Chinese mass-market sportswear wholesaler with a small premium-running growth engine, on fully SBC-expensed owner FCF with leases charged as operating cost, convertibles treated as converted, and every stripped income stream matched by its asset in the bridge. Roughly a third of the equity value is net cash and non-operating assets (deposits, associates, FVOCI stakes, the Ding-family KP receivable at a 30% haircut); the operating business is capitalised at a 13x terminal multiple, deliberately below the house 20x, because the core brand is ex-growth. The scenario weights, not the discount rate, carry the competitive and execution risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Core Xtep brand (87% of revenue) keeps declining faster than the guided 'slight' FY2026 drop; each 1pp of sustained adjusted EBITDA margin is worth roughly RMB100m of annual owner FCF.

Working capital: receivable days of 120-127 and inventory days of 105 are modelled as scaling with revenue CHANGE only; a structural stretch from distributor support would turn the base case's near-zero working-capital line into a recurring outflow.
The KP Convertible Bond (RMB1.02bn, ~RMB0.24/share at 70%) is a related-party receivable from a loss-making business; full write-off would remove ~HK$0.28/share.
Subsidy income (RMB301m, 2.1% of revenue, ~13% of adjusted EBITDA) is treated as recurring operating income; a policy change would cut the margin anchor by ~2pp.

Convertible dilution: if the share price stays below HK$5.23 to maturity the CBs are repaid in cash (2024 CB redeemable 2030, 2021 CB 2027, 2026 CB at 104.59% in 2029) -- the if-converted treatment then overstates the count and understates net debt by RMB1.27bn, which roughly offset each other near the strikes.
CNY/HKD rate: all values are RMB converted at 1.1727; a 5% RMB depreciation against the HKD peg cuts every HKD figure by 5%.
WACC built in CNY at 9.5%; the sensitivity grid shows the exposure if an HKD/USD-based investor demands more.
